title: disjoint-set union and connectivity maintenance
concepts: Disjoint-set union (DSU), also called union-find, maintains a partition of elements into non-overlapping equivalence classes and answers whether two elements share a component.
Find returns a representative for an element's set; union merges two sets only when their representatives differ.
Path compression rewrites nodes along a find path to point nearer the representative, while union by size or rank limits tree height during merges.
Together, path compression and union by size/rank give amortized O(α(n)) operation time, where inverse Ackermann α grows so slowly that it is effectively constant for practical input sizes.
DSU supports incremental edge additions and connectivity checks but does not naturally support deleting edges or enumerating a shortest path.
A failed union when adding an undirected edge indicates its endpoints were already connected, which can detect cycle creation in incremental connectivity settings.
Component metadata such as size can be stored at representatives and updated on union; representative identity itself has no semantic meaning.
Kruskal's minimum spanning tree algorithm uses DSU to reject edges that would connect vertices already in the same component.
